name: Question 20
problem:
A numerical method is used to approximate a solution to an initial value problem, resulting in the table below. If the exact solution is $y(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ find, rounded to three decimal places, the global truncation error at each step.

| $n$ | ${x}_{n}$ | ${y}_{n}$ | ${e}_{n}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.1$ | $0.099$ | {{field-1}} |
| $2$ | $0.3$ | $0.285$ | {{field-2}} |
| $3$ | $0.6$ | $0.540$ | {{field-3}} |
worked_solution:
The global truncation error (GTE) is the total error accumulated after several steps of a numerical method. The GTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from ${x}_{n-1}$ to ${x}_{n}={x}_{n-1}+Δx$ is

$$
{e}_{n}=y({x}_{n})-{y}_{n},
$$

where $y({x}_{n})$ is the exact value at ${x}_{n},$ and ${y}_{n}$ is the numerical value produced after $n$ steps.

We are given the numerical values ${y}_{n}$ produced at each step in the table. Now, we compute the exact value $y({x}_{n})$ at each value of ${x}_{n}:$

- The exact value at ${x}_{0}=0$ is $y(0)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)=0.$

- The exact value at ${x}_{1}=0.1$ is $y(0.1)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.1).$

- The exact value at ${x}_{2}=0.3$ is $y(0.3)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.3).$

- The exact value at ${x}_{3}=0.6$ is $y(0.6)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.6).$

Let's add these values to the table.

| $n$ | ${x}_{n}$ | ${y}_{n}$ | $y({x}_{n})$ | ${e}_{n}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.1$ | $0.099$ | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.1)$ |  |
| $2$ | $0.3$ | $0.285$ | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.3)$ |  |
| $3$ | $0.6$ | $0.540$ | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.6)$ |  |

Finally, we find the GTE at each step, rounding to three decimal places in each case:

- The GTE of the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}_{1} & =y({x}_{1})-{y}_{1} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.1)-0.099 \\  & ≈0.001.\end{aligned}
$$

- The GTE of the second step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}_{2} & =y({x}_{2})-{y}_{2} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.3)-0.285 \\  & ≈0.011.\end{aligned}
$$

- The GTE of the third step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}_{3} & =y({x}_{3})-{y}_{3} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.6)-0.540 \\  & ≈0.025.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed table is as given below.

| $n$ | ${x}_{n}$ | ${y}_{n}$ | $y({x}_{n})$ | ${e}_{n}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.1$ | $0.099$ | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.1)$ | $0.001$ |
| $2$ | $0.3$ | $0.285$ | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.3)$ | $0.011$ |
| $3$ | $0.6$ | $0.540$ | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.6)$ | $0.025$ |

Question 20
?
A numerical method is used to approximate a solution to an initial value problem, resulting in the table below. If the exact solution is y(x)=sin⁡x, find, rounded to three decimal places, the global truncation error at each step.
n xn yn en
0 0 0 0
1 0.1 0.099
0.001
2 0.3 0.285
0.011
3 0.6 0.540
0.025
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The global truncation error (GTE) is the total error accumulated after several steps of a numerical method. The GTE of a numerical method at step n from xn−1 to xn=xn−1+Δx is en=y(xn)−yn, where y(xn) is the exact value at xn, and yn is the numerical value produced after n steps.

We are given the numerical values yn produced at each step in the table. Now, we compute the exact value y(xn) at each value of xn:

  • The exact value at x0=0 is y(0)=sin⁡(0)=0.

  • The exact value at x1=0.1 is y(0.1)=sin⁡(0.1).

  • The exact value at x2=0.3 is y(0.3)=sin⁡(0.3).

  • The exact value at x3=0.6 is y(0.6)=sin⁡(0.6).

Let's add these values to the table.

n xn yn y(xn) en
0 0 0 0 0
1 0.1 0.099 sin⁡(0.1)
2 0.3 0.285 sin⁡(0.3)
3 0.6 0.540 sin⁡(0.6)

Finally, we find the GTE at each step, rounding to three decimal places in each case:

  • The GTE of the first step is e1=y(x1)−y1=sin⁡(0.1)−0.099≈0.001.

  • The GTE of the second step is e2=y(x2)−y2=sin⁡(0.3)−0.285≈0.011.

  • The GTE of the third step is e3=y(x3)−y3=sin⁡(0.6)−0.540≈0.025.

Therefore, the completed table is as given below.

n xn yn y(xn) en
0 0 0 0 0
1 0.1 0.099 sin⁡(0.1) 0.001
2 0.3 0.285 sin⁡(0.3) 0.011
3 0.6 0.540 sin⁡(0.6) 0.025
